programmes.source_snippet: Singapore Citizen students aged 7–16 receive annual Edusave contributions, and students can receive Edusave awards such as the Edusave Merit Bursary, Edusave Good Progress Award and Edusave Awards for Achievement, Good Leadership and Service.

programmes.amount_note: Tiered fee subsidy: 100% (GHI ≤ $4,000/PCI ≤ $1,000) stepping down to 33% (GHI $9,001–$12,000); top tiers include free textbooks/attire, $21/month transport subsidy, meal subsidies and a $1,600 pre-university bursary

procedure_steps.detail: Apply through the independent school with household income documents

eligibility.income_note: SC students in independent schools; gross household income up to $12,000/month for partial subsidy

programmes.source_snippet: Singapore Citizen students in independent schools receive tiered school-fee subsidies based on gross household income — 100% subsidy plus free textbooks, transport and meal subsidies for households earning ≤ $4,000/month (or PCI ≤ $1,000).

programmes.amount_note: Government top-ups are announced in Budgets (e.g. Edusave/PSEA top-ups under cost-of-living packages); funds can be used for approved courses at post-secondary education institutions

procedure_steps.detail: No application needed — this is paid automatically to everyone who qualifies. Check that the authority holds your current address and bank details; a missing detail is the usual reason an automatic payment does not arrive.

eligibility.income_note: All Singapore Citizens of school-going age; usage for the account holder's or siblings' approved post-secondary education

programmes.source_snippet: The PSEA is opened automatically for every Singapore Citizen child; balances from Edusave and the Child Development Account roll into it, and the Government has made top-ups to PSEA in Budget packages; funds pay approved fees at post-secondary institutions.

programmes.amount_note: One-off opening credit of $500; does not expire; a time-limited $500 top-up from 2020 expired 31 December 2025

procedure_steps.detail: Log in to MySkillsFuture portal with Singpass, select an eligible course and submit a credit claim

eligibility.income_note: All Singapore Citizens aged 25+; not means-tested

programmes.source_snippet: All Singapore Citizens aged 25 and above receive a SkillsFuture Credit base tier of $500 (which does not expire) to offset out-of-pocket course fees for a wide range of approved skills-related courses.

programmes.amount_note: $4,000 top-up for Singapore Citizens aged 40+, usable for selected employability-focused courses (about 7,000 courses); does not expire

procedure_steps.detail: Log in to MySkillsFuture portal with Singpass and claim against an eligible SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) course

eligibility.income_note: All Singapore Citizens aged 40+; not means-tested

programmes.source_snippet: On 1 May 2024, the remaining credit balance from the Additional SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career Support) was merged with the top-up of $4,000 to form the new SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career).

programmes.amount_note: Training allowance of up to $3,000/month (based on 50% of average income, capped) for up to 24 months for selected full-time courses; plus the $4,000 mid-career credit

procedure_steps.detail: Enrol in an eligible full-time course and apply for the training allowance via MySkillsFuture

eligibility.income_note: Singapore Citizens aged 40+ taking selected full-time courses

programmes.source_snippet: Under the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme, mid-career Singaporeans aged 40 and above receive the $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top-up and a training allowance when they take up selected full-time courses.

programmes.amount_note: Salary support of up to 90% (capped) for place-and-train CCPs for long-term unemployed or mature jobseekers, and course fee subsidies; exact rates by programme

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via participating employers or WSG's careers portal for advertised CCP places

eligibility.income_note: Singapore Citizens/PRs; mid-career jobseekers and workers at risk of redundancy

programmes.source_snippet: Career Conversion Programmes help mid-career individuals reskill and switch into new occupations or sectors, with employers receiving salary support and course fee subsidies for the reskilling period.

programmes.amount_note: $10,000 credit per eligible employer, covering up to 90% of out-of-pocket costs on SFEC-supported programmes and courses

eligibility.income_note: Employers that meet SFEC eligibility criteria (e.g. contributed to SDF and employed SC/PR workers in the qualifying period)

programmes.source_snippet: The SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit provides eligible employers a one-off $10,000 credit to cover up to 90% of out-of-pocket expenses for enterprise transformation and workforce transformation programmes.

programmes.amount_note: Subsidised fibre broadband from a few dollars a month and co-payment for devices based on means-testing; households on ComCare assistance may receive enhanced support

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via digitalaccess.gov.sg or call 6377 3800

eligibility.income_note: IMDA DigitalAccess@Home sets the outer income ceiling at monthly gross household income of SGD 3,400 (SGD 40,800/year) or per capita income of SGD 900/month, and this higher band applies only to households with a primary-school student or a person with disabilities. The base band is GHI SGD 1,900/month (SGD 22,800/year). Income is averaged over the last 12 months.

programmes.source_snippet: DigitalAccess@Home provides subsidised broadband and/or laptop/tablet bundles to low-income households with school-going children or persons with disabilities.

programmes.amount_note: Up to $120,000 (families) or $60,000 (singles 35+) for new or resale flats, tiered by average gross monthly household income (≤ $9,000 for families); credited to CPF Ordinary Account

procedure_steps.detail: Apply for an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter on the HDB Flat Portal
Grant eligibility and quantum are assessed with your flat application

documents_required.doc: Income documents for 12 months prior to application

eligibility.income_note: First-timer SC household; average gross monthly household income ≤ $9,000 (families) / ≤ $4,500 (singles); at least one applicant in continuous employment

programmes.source_snippet: Eligible first-timer households can receive up to $120,000, depending on your household income; eligible first-timer single citizens up to $60,000.

programmes.name_local: CPF Housing Grant for Resale Flats (Families)
programmes.name_en: CPF Housing Grant for Resale Flats (Families)
programmes.amount_note: $80,000 (2- to 4-room resale) or $50,000 (5-room or larger); stackable with EHG and Proximity Housing Grant up to $230,000 total

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via HDB Flat Portal with HFE letter when submitting resale application

eligibility.income_note: First-timer SC family nucleus; average gross monthly household income ≤ $14,000; remaining lease conditions apply

programmes.source_snippet: First-timer couples buying a resale HDB flat can receive the CPF Housing Grant for Resale Flats (Families) of up to $80,000 for four-room or smaller resale flats, and $50,000 for five-room or larger resale flats.

programmes.amount_note: $30,000 (live with parents/child) or $20,000 (within 4km); for families buying resale flats; $15,000/$10,000 for eligible singles

procedure_steps.detail: Indicate PHG in the resale flat application via HDB Flat Portal

eligibility.income_note: No income ceiling. HDB's 2026 eligibility table for the Proximity Housing Grant lists only citizenship, age 21+, not having taken the grant before, the parent/child proximity or co-living condition, and remaining lease over 20 years. Income does not appear as a criterion, unlike the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant.

programmes.source_snippet: You may receive a Proximity Housing Grant of $20,000 if you buy a resale flat to live near (within 4km of) your parents or child, or $30,000 if you buy a resale flat to live with your parents or child.

programmes.name_local: CPF Housing Grant for Resale Flats (Singles)
programmes.amount_note: $40,000 (2- to 4-room) or $25,000 (5-room); stackable with EHG (Singles) up to $60,000 and PHG

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via HDB Flat Portal with HFE letter

eligibility.income_note: Single SC first-timer; average gross monthly income ≤ $7,000

programmes.source_snippet: Eligible first-timer single citizens aged 35 and above buying a resale flat can receive the CPF Housing Grant for Resale Flats (Singles) of up to $40,000 for 2- to 4-room flats and $25,000 for 5-room flats.

programmes.amount_note: $15,000 credited to CPF Ordinary Account for the purchase of a 3-room flat in a non-mature estate

procedure_steps.detail: Apply with your flat application; eligibility assessed by HDB

eligibility.income_note: Second-timer SC families (with at least one SC child) in 2-room subsidised/rental flats buying a 3-room new flat; income ceilings apply

programmes.source_snippet: The Step-Up CPF Housing Grant of $15,000 helps second-timer families living in public rental flats or 2-room subsidised flats buy a 3-room new flat in a non-mature estate.

programmes.amount_note: Proceeds (depends on flat value and lease sold) are used to top up the CPF Retirement Account to the prevailing retirement sum and join CPF LIFE; an LBS bonus of $5,000–$30,000 by flat type applies when the required RA top-up is met

procedure_steps.detail: Make an e-appointment with HDB for a preliminary financial counselling session
Choose retained lease based on youngest owner's age; application takes about 3 months

eligibility.income_note: All owners aged 65+ (at least one SC); household income ≤ $14,000/month; fulfilled 5-year MOP; flat has at least 20 years of lease to sell

programmes.source_snippet: Provides seniors with a steady stream of retirement income when they sell the tail-end of their flat lease to HDB while they continue to occupy the flat for the lease they retained.

programmes.amount_note: Cash bonus of up to $30,000 depending on the top-up made to the CPF Retirement Account from the sale proceeds

procedure_steps.detail: Apply when selling your flat and buying a smaller one; HDB assesses the bonus with the transactions

eligibility.income_note: At least one SC owner aged 55+; household income ≤ $14,000/month; right-sizing to a 3-room or smaller flat

programmes.source_snippet: The Silver Housing Bonus gives elderly households a cash bonus of up to $30,000 when they right-size to a smaller HDB flat and use part of the sale proceeds to top up their CPF Retirement Account and join CPF LIFE.

programmes.amount_note: Essential improvement items fully government-funded; optional items subsidised up to 95% — owners pay a few hundred to about $1,500+ depending on flat type (SC households)

procedure_steps.detail: No application needed — this is paid automatically to everyone who qualifies. Check that the authority holds your current address and bank details; a missing detail is the usual reason an automatic payment does not arrive.

eligibility.income_note: SC owners of HDB flats built in or before 1997 in precincts selected for HIP; PR households pay full cost

programmes.source_snippet: Under the Home Improvement Programme, HDB renovates ageing flats (built up to 1997); the Government fully pays for essential improvements and heavily subsidises optional items, with flat owners paying only a small share.

programmes.amount_note: Second-timer families: Fresh Start Housing Grant of up to $75,000 ($60,000 upfront + $15,000 deferred over 5 years, subject to annual social assessment); first-timers receive EHG up to $120,000; resale levy capped at $30,000

procedure_steps.detail: Obtain a Letter of Social Assessment (LSA) via your ComLink+/social service agency
Apply for a 2-room Flexi or 3-room Standard flat (45–65 year lease) during HDB sales exercises within 1 year of LSA

eligibility.income_note: ComLink+ families in HDB rental flats; average gross monthly household income ≤ $7,000; at least one applicant in continuous employment for 12 months; 20-year MOP applies

programmes.source_snippet: Second-timers will receive the Fresh Start Housing Grant (FSHG)... Applications made from Jul 2025 sales exercise: upfront disbursement before key collection $60,000; disbursement after key collection over 5 years up to $15,000; total grant amount $75,000.

programmes.amount_note: Heavily subsidised monthly rent scaled to household income and flat type (from around $26–$33/month for the lowest-income tier); income guideline of $1,500/month household income, assessed holistically

procedure_steps.detail: Apply at an HDB branch office with household and income documents

eligibility.income_note: SC household (family nucleus or joint singles) aged 21+; household income guideline of $1,500/month (flexible, case-by-case); no property ownership

programmes.source_snippet: HDB's Public Rental Scheme provides heavily subsidised 1-room and 2-room rental flats for lower-income Singapore Citizen households who have no other housing options; rents are tiered by household income.

programmes.funder: Ministry of Transport (MOT) / Public Transport Council
programmes.amount_note: $60 voucher per eligible household under the 2025 PTV Exercise, redeemable in $10 denominations to top up travel cards
programmes.deadline_note: 2025 PTV Exercise applications: 20 Jan 2026 – 31 Oct 2026; households from the previous exercise are auto-notified in Stage 1

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via go.gov.sg/ptv or in person at any Community Centre/Club
Redeem voucher to any household member's travel card at ticket machines/offices

eligibility.income_note: Monthly household income per person ≤ $1,800; at least one SC/PR household member

programmes.source_snippet: Following the implementation of a fare adjustment from 27 December 2025, the Government has made available PTVs worth $60 each for resident households with monthly household income per person of not more than $1,800, as part of the 2025 PTV Exercise.

programmes.amount_note: Concessionary per-trip fares (roughly half of adult fares); hybrid monthly concession pass available for unlimited basic bus and train rides

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via TransitLink (online or at concession card replacement offices); card mailed to you

eligibility.income_note: SC/PR aged 60+; not means-tested

programmes.source_snippet: Singapore Citizens and PRs aged 60 and above travel at concessionary fares on basic bus and train services with the Senior Citizen Concession Card; monthly concession passes are also available.

programmes.amount_note: Concessionary fares and monthly passes; primary school pupils may travel free on basic services with the Child Concession Card

eligibility.income_note: Full-time students at approved institutions; not means-tested

programmes.source_snippet: Eligible students pay concessionary fares on basic bus and train services, with monthly concession passes and the Bus Pass/Train Pass options for unlimited travel.

programmes.funder: Land Transport Authority (LTA) / TransitLink / SG Enable
programmes.amount_note: Concessionary fares; from 2025 eligible PWD concession cardholders enjoy free travel on basic bus and train services (announced as part of the fare concession enhancements)

eligibility.income_note: SC/PR with permanent disability certified via SG Enable; not means-tested

programmes.source_snippet: Persons with disabilities can travel at concessionary fares on basic bus and train services with the PWD Concession Card; a monthly concession pass is available and travel for eligible PWDs on basic services is free from 6 July 2025 under the enhanced scheme.

programmes.amount_note: Up to 15% discount off adult fares; monthly hybrid concession pass option

eligibility.income_note: WIS recipients (lower-wage SC workers); not separately means-tested

programmes.source_snippet: Lower-wage workers receiving Workfare Income Supplement enjoy up to 15% off adult fares on basic bus and train services with the Workfare Transport Concession Card; a monthly WTC hybrid pass is also available.

programmes.name_local: Taxi Subsidy Scheme (for persons with disabilities)
programmes.funder: SG Enable / Ministry of Social and Family Development
programmes.amount_note: Means-tested percentage subsidy of taxi fares for approved trips to school or employment

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via SG Enable with disability certification and proof of school/work attendance

eligibility.income_note: SC/PR with certified disability who cannot use public transport; means-tested

programmes.source_snippet: The Taxi Subsidy Scheme provides means-tested subsidies for taxi travel to persons with disabilities who need to take taxis to school or work because they cannot use public transport or drive.

programmes.amount_note: Up to 50% of qualifying costs for pre-approved solutions; annual cap of $30,000 per company per financial year

procedure_steps.detail: Get a quotation from a pre-approved vendor listed on GoBusiness
Submit application on the Business Grants Portal before signing/paying the vendor
After approval, deploy the solution and submit claims with usage report

eligibility.income_note: SME registered and operating in Singapore; ≥30% local shareholding; group annual turnover ≤ $100m or ≤200 employees

programmes.source_snippet: The PSG supports local SMEs in adopting pre-approved IT solutions and equipment, providing up to 50% funding support for qualifying costs, capped at $30,000 per company per financial year.

programmes.amount_note: Funds up to 50% of qualifying project costs for SMEs (higher support for sustainability-related projects), assessed per project on the Business Grants Portal

procedure_steps.detail: Develop a project proposal and apply on the Business Grants Portal with CorpPass

eligibility.income_note: Company registered and operating in Singapore, ≥30% local shareholding, financially able to complete the project

programmes.source_snippet: The Enterprise Development Grant supports Singapore companies in projects that upgrade, innovate or venture overseas — funding a share of qualifying project costs such as consultancy, manpower, and software and equipment.

programmes.amount_note: Up to 50% of eligible costs, capped at $100,000 per company per new market

procedure_steps.detail: Apply on the Business Grants Portal before commencing the overseas market activity

eligibility.income_note: SME criteria; new-to-market (limited prior overseas sales in the target market)

programmes.source_snippet: The MRA grant supports SMEs taking their first steps overseas, funding up to 50% of eligible costs capped at $100,000 per company per new market, covering overseas market promotion, business development and set-up.

programmes.amount_note: Grant of $20,000–$50,000 on a 1:1 basis: founders must inject matching paid-up capital (at least 50% as paid-up capital; co-matching may come from AMP/third-party investment); mentorship from Accredited Mentor Partners included

procedure_steps.detail: Pitch to an Accredited Mentor Partner (AMP) and obtain a letter of recommendation
AMP submits the application to Enterprise Singapore; inject co-matching capital

eligibility.income_note: First-time SC/PR founder(s) collectively holding ≥30% equity; company registered as private limited for less than 6 months; at least two applicants

programmes.source_snippet: With effect from 1 April 2024, EnterpriseSG will support all successful startup grant recipients on a 1:1 support ratio, for a grant amount from S$20,000 to S$50,000.

programmes.amount_note: Competitive grants of up to $250,000 (Proof-of-Concept) and up to $500,000 (Proof-of-Value), with milestone-based disbursement and matching requirements

procedure_steps.detail: Submit proposal via Startup SG portal during grant calls

eligibility.income_note: Singapore-registered startups with proprietary technology and scalability; company and shareholding conditions apply

programmes.source_snippet: Startup SG Tech fast-tracks the development of proprietary technology solutions with Proof-of-Concept (POC) and Proof-of-Value (POV) grants for startups with innovative and scalable technologies.

programmes.amount_note: Government co-investment matched to third-party investor funding; investment caps by sector and stage as published by EnterpriseSG

procedure_steps.detail: Raise from a qualified third-party investor who applies for co-investment

eligibility.income_note: Singapore-based startups with innovative technology, assessed by co-investors

programmes.source_snippet: Under Startup SG Equity, the Government co-invests with independent, qualified third-party investors into eligible Singapore-based technology startups, on a shared-risk basis.

programmes.amount_note: Government risk-share of up to 70% on loans from participating financial institutions; loan caps vary by EFS loan type (e.g. SME Working Capital Loan, Trade Loan, Fixed Assets Loan)

procedure_steps.detail: Apply for an EFS loan directly with a participating bank or financial institution

eligibility.income_note: Singapore-registered companies; SME criteria and ≥30% local shareholding for most EFS components

programmes.source_snippet: The Enterprise Financing Scheme enables Singapore enterprises to access financing more readily across growth stages — Government shares the loan default risk with participating financial institutions for SME working capital, trade, fixed assets, venture debt and mergers & acquisitions loans.

programmes.amount_note: Up to 70% support for pre-approved energy-efficient equipment, capped per company per year (base tier); enhanced tier for larger investments

procedure_steps.detail: Apply on the Business Grants Portal before purchasing the pre-approved equipment

eligibility.income_note: Local businesses in eligible sectors; SME criteria apply for the enhanced tier

programmes.source_snippet: The Energy Efficiency Grant supports local businesses in the food services, food manufacturing and retail sectors (extended to more sectors) to adopt energy-efficient equipment, co-funding up to 70% of qualifying costs.

programmes.amount_note: Up to 80% of qualifying costs for pre-approved automation equipment, capped at $5,000 per stall over 3 years

procedure_steps.detail: Check the pre-approved equipment list and submit claims with proof of purchase via the appointed administrator

eligibility.income_note: NEA-licensed hawkers (cooked food stallholders)

programmes.source_snippet: The Hawkers' Productivity Grant co-funds hawkers' purchase of automation and productivity equipment (e.g. dishwashers, ordering systems), covering up to 80% of qualifying equipment costs capped at $5,000 over three years.

programmes.amount_note: Free-of-charge career guidance, workshops and job matching

eligibility.income_note: No income test published. WSG's Careers Connect describes open career coaching, advisory and job-matching services for jobseekers and workers; no income criterion appears on the official page (last modified August 2026).

programmes.source_snippet: Careers Connect centres and WSG's career matching services provide free career coaching, job search assistance and access to job fairs for Singaporeans seeking employment or career changes.

programmes.funder: Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) / IRAS
programmes.amount_note: Wage credit of up to 20–30% of the employee's monthly wage (capped, e.g. up to $400/month in the initial period), paid automatically to eligible employers based on CPF data

procedure_steps.detail: No application needed — this is paid automatically to everyone who qualifies. Check that the authority holds your current address and bank details; a missing detail is the usual reason an automatic payment does not arrive.

eligibility.income_note: For employers hiring SC/PR persons with disabilities; paid to employer, no application needed

programmes.source_snippet: The Enabling Employment Credit is a wage offset for employers who hire Singaporean persons with disabilities, co-funding part of the employee's wages for a period to support sustained employment.

programmes.funder: SG Enable / Ministry of Social and Family Development
programmes.amount_note: Grants co-funding up to 90% of costs for components such as apprenticeship, job redesign and workplace modifications, subject to published caps

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via SG Enable before incurring costs

eligibility.income_note: Employers hiring SC/PR persons with disabilities

programmes.source_snippet: The Open Door Programme provides funding support to employers who hire, train and integrate persons with disabilities — covering recruitment, training, job redesign and workplace modification costs.

programmes.amount_note: Compensation amounts are set by statute: medical leave wages, medical expenses, and lump-sum payments for permanent incapacity or death, subject to WICA caps

procedure_steps.detail: Report the accident to your employer as soon as possible
Employer notifies MOM and its WIC insurer; claim is processed by the insurer, with MOM dispute resolution if needed

eligibility.income_note: All employees covered (manual and non-manual, regardless of salary); excludes domestic workers, uniformed services and self-employed

programmes.source_snippet: Under WICA, employees (or their dependants) can claim compensation from the employer's mandatory work injury insurance for injuries or diseases arising out of and in the course of employment, without needing to prove fault.

programmes.amount_note: Free or nominal-cost legal aid and representation for qualifying civil cases

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online or at LAB; undergo means test (income/assets) and merits test

eligibility.income_note: Legal Aid Bureau means test in force from 1 April 2024: average per capita gross monthly household income must be SGD 1,050 or lower over the preceding 12 months. For a single-person household that is SGD 12,600/year; for a household of N people the ceiling is N x SGD 12,600. Separate capital tests also apply.

programmes.source_snippet: The Legal Aid Bureau provides legal aid, advice and representation in civil matters to persons of limited means who satisfy the means and merits tests, at no or nominal cost.
